answer: To resist sybil attacks, agent economies can require each new identity to post a slashable bond and complete a unique resource-bound task, such as proving contribution to sustainable timber management around a monitored lagoon, anchored by a non-transferable knoll of zero-knowledge hardware attestation. This raises attacker costs because scaling fakes demands continuous real capital and compute that cannot be amortized cheaply across identities, while honest agents maintain standing with modest ongoing effort.
